**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The white square plate is about 25 cm across. Its area is roughly 25 × 25 ≈ 600 cm² (rounded corners reduce this slightly, so I use about 600 cm²).

**STEP 3 - Items:** Arugula leaves and stems, lightly dressed or glossy in places. There is a tiny orange fleck, possibly shredded carrot, which is negligible. No clear oil pool is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The leaves cover about 25% of the plate (about 150 cm²). The rest is bare white plate.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Loose leafy greens have a bulk density of about 0.15 g/ml. 450 ml × 0.15 ≈ 68 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Raw arugula is about 25 kcal/100 g. 68 g × 25 kcal/100 g ≈ 17 kcal. The carrot fleck adds only about 1 kcal, so I leave it out of the total.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A single-layer pile of loose arugula covering about a quarter of a dinner plate, roughly 70 g, is plausible. It is a light side salad, and the energy is low, as expected for leafy greens without dressing or other additions.
